Plot dissimilarity against overlap of sample pairs

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotDOC.R, R/zzz-mae.R
plotDOC.Rd

plotDOC() draws the dissimilarity of each pair of samples against their overlap, with a smooth: the dissimilarity-overlap curve (DOC). A falling curve at high overlap suggests that the same taxa behave alike in different communities.

Usage

plotDOC(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
plotDOC(
  x,
  overlap,
  dissimilarity,
  group = NULL,
  pairs = c("all", "within", "between"),
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotDOC(x, ..., experiment = 1L)

Arguments

x

a SummarizedExperiment object.

...

additional arguments passed to geom_point.

overlap, dissimilarity

Character scalar. Specify the sample by sample matrices in metadata(x), as stored by mia::addDissimilarity(): the overlap on the x axis and the dissimilarity on the y axis.

group

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that identifies subjects, needed for pairs = "within" and "between". (Default: NULL)

pairs

Character scalar. Draws all pairs of samples ("all"), pairs from the same subject ("within") or from different subjects ("between"). (Default: "all")

experiment

Character scalar or integer scalar. For a MultiAssayExperiment, the experiment to plot; its samples get the colData of x. (Default: 1L)

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Each pair of samples is drawn once, with the robust LOWESS curve of Bashan et al. (2016); above 1000 pairs, points are drawn with transparency. In Bashan et al. (2016), overlap is mia's "overlap" of relative abundances and dissimilarity is the root Jensen-Shannon divergence of the shared taxa, renormalised; mia's "jsd" uses all taxa.

References

Bashan A, et al. (2016). Universality of human microbial dynamics. Nature 534(7606):259-262.

Examples

# Samples of four artificial guts
data("SilvermanAGutData", package = "miaTime")
tse <- SilvermanAGutData
# Five samples have no reads
tse <- tse[, colSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(tse)) > 0]
tse <- mia::transformAssay(tse, method = "relabundance")
tse <- mia::addDissimilarity(tse, method = "overlap",
    assay.type = "relabundance")
tse <- mia::addDissimilarity(tse, method = "jsd",
    assay.type = "relabundance")
plotDOC(tse, overlap = "overlap", dissimilarity = "jsd",
    group = "Vessel", pairs = "between")
